lessons.title: Right triangles and calculator modes
lessons.objective: Use right-triangle geometry and side ratios, recover acute angles, and keep angle units and calculator modes consistent.
workedExamples: Keep the hypotenuse fixed while the reference angle changes
Preserve an exact hypotenuse and group a missing-leg calculation
Match equivalent angles to their calculator modes
Solve a right triangular panel from an angle and its hypotenuse
Recover an acute angle from two legs
lessons.guided: Retain the source's side-role, exact-length, and calculator guided work.

interaction.purpose: Predict the entered sine value, change DEG/RAD without silently changing input, repair the mismatch, and scale the triangle while retaining its ratio.

mistakes: Choose the hypotenuse from orientation
Ignore the right-angle marker
Use the side opposite the right angle, then relabel the legs relative to the reference angle.
Convert a sine result between units
Confuse an angle with a dimensionless ratio
Convert the input angle or change the calculator mode.
Use the negative root as a side
Forget the geometric domain
Lengths are positive and the hypotenuse must remain longest.
lessons.acceptance: A checkpoint requires Pythagorean grouping and recovered acute angle, side solving, both exact angle conversions, and mode repair.

lessons.title: Radians, the unit circle, and exact values
lessons.objective: Locate directed angles, evaluate all six trigonometric ratios with correct signs and domains, and use radians in circular measurements.
lessons.source: Original F04 instruction; overlap with planned MTH 215 m06-l01, m06-l03, m06-l04 is recorded without claiming those lessons exist.
scope: Signed unit-circle coordinates and reference angles
Arc length, sector area, and angular/linear speed
workedExamples: Reduce -495 degrees to 225 degrees with reference angle 45 degrees
At 210 degrees derive sine, cosine, and tangent from coordinates
At -pi/2 classify csc, sec, and cot rather than dividing by zero
Radius 3 m and angle 5pi/6: arc 5pi/2 m and sector area 15pi/4 m²
Two revolutions in 5 s at radius 3 m: angular speed 4pi/5 rad/s and linear speed 12pi/5 m/s
lessons.guided: At 150 degrees supply exact sine, cosine, and tangent, then use the angle in an arc calculation.

interaction.purpose: Choose directed angles and predict exact sine/cosine before checking coordinates. Compare signs, coterminal positions, axis cases, and a text coordinate table.

mistakes: Use acute signs everywhere
Carry triangle positivity beyond quadrant I
Read the x and y signs of the terminal point.
Report zero for an undefined reciprocal
Treat division by zero like zero divided by a number
Identify the denominator and decide definedness before evaluating.
Use degrees directly in s=r theta
Recall the formula without its unit condition
Convert the angle to radians before multiplying by radius.
lessons.acceptance: Required questions cover directed angles and references, direct ratios, reciprocal domain cases, and a combined circular-measure checkpoint for arc length, sector area, angular speed, and tangential speed.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal graphs, phase, and inverse values
lessons.objective: Interpret sinusoidal amplitude, period, midline, and phase in angular and time models, and select inverse-trigonometric principal values.
lessons.source: Original F04 instruction; extends F03 transformations and inverse-domain reasoning.
scope: Period and phase after factoring the input
Angular frequency versus cycles per second
Inverse sine/cosine/tangent domains and principal ranges
Principal inverse values versus full equation solutions
workedExamples: For y=-3 sin(2(x-pi/4))+1 recover amplitude 3, period pi, shift pi/4, range [-2,4], and five cycle anchors
For y=2 cos(3(x+pi/6))-1 identify the negative phase shift and period 2pi/3
For v(t)=2 sin(4pi t-pi/2)+1 V find frequency 2 Hz, period 1/2 s, and delay 1/8 s
Evaluate arcsin(sin(5pi/6)), arccos(cos(7pi/6)), and arctan(tan(3pi/4)) using their principal ranges
Reject arcsin(6/5) over the reals and distinguish inverse sine from reciprocal sine
lessons.guided: Read a negative-amplitude sine model and recover an inverse value outside the principal input interval.

interaction.purpose: Change signed amplitude, frequency multiplier, phase, offset, and sine/cosine choice. Predict amplitude, exact period, and starting value; verify five accessible quarter-cycle points and the graph.

mistakes: Use a negative amplitude
Confuse distance from midline with orientation
Amplitude is the absolute outside coefficient; its sign controls reflection.
Use the raw phase constant as the shift
Skip factoring the angular coefficient
Solve for the input that makes the phase zero.
Return the original angle from every inverse composition
Ignore the restricted range
Choose the coterminal/reflected representative in the inverse function's principal range.
lessons.acceptance: Checkpoint answers require angular and time periods with units, correct phase, a quarter-cycle value, all three inverse principal values, and the inverse-sine domain restriction.

lessons.title: Identities and complete trigonometric solutions
lessons.objective: Use foundational, sum, and double-angle identities with domain restrictions and return every solution in a stated interval without losing zero factors.
lessons.source: Original F04 instruction; reuses exact-number and unordered real-set graders.
scope: Identity validity on the original domain
Principal solution versus every periodic branch
Factoring without division by a possibly zero trigonometric factor
workedExamples: With sin theta=3/5 in quadrant II, find cos theta=-4/5 and tan theta=-3/4
Simplify (1-cos² theta)/sin theta but retain sin theta nonzero
Derive sin75=(sqrt6+sqrt2)/4 from the addition identity
Use sin theta=3/5 and cos theta=-4/5 to obtain sin2theta=-24/25 and cos2theta=7/25
Solve sin theta=1/2 on [0,360) and describe the two all-real angle families
Solve sin(2theta)=1/2 on [0,360) to obtain 15,75,195,255 degrees
Factor sin theta(2sin theta-1)=0 and retain 0,30,150,180 degrees
lessons.guided: Recover all solutions to a factored sine equation, explaining why dividing by sine would lose solutions.

interaction.purpose: Choose sine/cosine, a target value, and an open/closed upper endpoint. Predict the full solution set and inspect candidate positions, including empty sets and the extra 360-degree endpoint.

mistakes: Claim an identity at an excluded angle
Simplification hides a zero denominator
Retain the original definedness condition.
Distribute sine across addition
Treat a nonlinear function as linear
Use the sum identity or a counterexample.
Keep only a calculator's principal angle
Stop before considering symmetry and periods
Generate every branch and filter by the stated interval.
Divide by sine and lose zero solutions
Apply a nonreversible algebraic step
Factor and solve each factor, then check the original equation.
lessons.acceptance: Four required questions combine identity domain reasoning, sum and double-angle values, frequency-scaled full roots, and zero-preserving factorization.
